# Plots with ggplot2 {#sec-plots}

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
```

Every plot starts with the same structure:

```r
ggplot(data, aes(x = ..., y = ...)) +
  geom_*()
```

- `aes()` maps **columns** to things you can see (x, y, color, fill, size)
- **Each layer is added with a `+` at the end of the line**
- Pick the geom by the types of variables (more in [Choosing a Plot](models.qmd#choosing-a-plot))

## Quick Reference: Geoms

| Use Case                                       | Function             | Variables                     |
|:-----------------------------------------------|:---------------------|:------------------------------|
| **Histogram**: distribution of one number      | `geom_histogram()`   | 1 numerical                   |
| **Boxplot**: spread and outliers               | `geom_boxplot()`     | 1 numerical (+ 1 categorical) |
| **Bar graph**: count each category             | `geom_bar()`         | 1 categorical                 |
| **Scatterplot**: relationship between two numbers | `geom_point()`    | 2 numerical                   |
| **Jittered points**: overlapping points spread out | `geom_jitter()`  | 2 numerical or 1 cat. + 1 num. |
| **Count plot**: point size = number of overlaps | `geom_count()`      | 2 discrete (e.g. ratings 1–5) |
| **Trend line** through a scatterplot           | `geom_smooth()`      | 2 numerical                   |
| **Reference line** at a value                  | `geom_vline()` / `geom_hline()` | any                |
| **Small multiples**: one panel per group       | `facet_wrap(~ group)` | any + 1 categorical          |

### Examples

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
# Histogram: play around with binwidth
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = hwy)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 3)

# Boxplot of one variable
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = hwy)) +
  geom_boxplot()

# Bar graph: counts each category for you
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = class)) +
  geom_bar()

# Boxplot comparing a number across categories
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = class, y = hwy)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  coord_flip() # flip so long category names don't overlap
```

## Trend Lines (`geom_smooth()`) {#trend-lines}

*From the Day 5 EDA activity*

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(subtitle = "Blue: straight line (lm). Red: LOESS curve")
```

| Argument            | What it does                                                         |
|:--------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `method = "lm"`     | Straight line of best fit (a linear model, see [Models](models.qmd)) |
| `method = "loess"`  | Flexible curve that follows the local pattern (the default for small data) |
| `se = FALSE`        | Removes the gray confidence band around the line                     |
| `formula = y ~ x`   | Spells out the formula and silences the "using formula" message      |

- !! If the straight line and the curve disagree (like above for big engines), a single straight line is a poor summary
- `stat_smooth()` does the same thing as `geom_smooth()`

## Overplotting: Jitter, Transparency, Count

*From the Day 8 activity.* When values are whole numbers (ratings 1–5), hundreds of points land on the same spot and the plot hides how many there are.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = cyl, y = hwy)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "geom_jitter() + alpha")

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = cyl, y = hwy)) +
  geom_count() +
  labs(title = "geom_count()")
```

- `geom_jitter(width =, height =)` nudges each point a little at random so stacks spread out
  - !! Jitter only changes where points are **drawn**, not the data. Set `height = 0` when the y values must stay exact
- `alpha = 0.4` makes points see-through: darker spots = more points
- `geom_count()` keeps points in place and sizes them by count. Downside: people judge areas poorly

## Reference Lines and Axis Limits

*From HW1*

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(mpg$displ), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(mpg$hwy), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 50))
```

- `geom_vline(xintercept =)` draws a vertical line; `geom_hline(yintercept =)` draws a horizontal one
- `mpg$hwy` pulls one column out of a data frame as a vector (needed here because the line isn't inside `aes()`)
- `scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 50))` sets the axis range. Starting at 0 avoids exaggerating differences

## Quick Reference: Plot Styling

| Use Case                                         | Function                           | Example                                     |
|:-------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Add a title, subtitle and axis labels            | `labs()`                           | see the chunk below                         |
| Rename the legend                                | `labs(fill = )` / `labs(color = )` | `labs(fill = "Fare Class")`                 |
| Color by a variable                              | `aes(color = )` / `aes(fill = )`   | `aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = class)`    |
| Choose a color for each category (bars)          | `scale_fill_manual()`              | see the chunk below                         |
| Choose a color for each category (points, lines) | `scale_color_manual()`             | see the chunk below                         |
| List R's color names                             | `colors()`                         | Run in the Console; hex codes work too: `"#4682B4"` |
| Change the overall look                          | `theme_*()`                        | `theme_minimal()`, `theme_bw()`, `theme_classic()` |
| Save a plot as an object                         | `<-`                               | `my_plot <- ggplot(mpg, aes(x = class)) + geom_bar()` |
| Export a plot as an image file                   | `ggsave()`                         | `ggsave("mpg-plot.png", plot = my_plot)`    |

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = drv)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("4" = "steelblue", "f" = "tomato", "r" = "gray40")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Engine size and fuel economy",
    x = "Displacement (L)",
    y = "Highway mpg",
    color = "Drive train"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

`scale_fill_manual()` works the same way for bars (from the Titanic activity):

```r
scale_fill_manual(values = c("First" = "cornflowerblue",
                             "Second" = "mediumvioletred",
                             "Third" = "darkgoldenrod1"))
```
